intelligence.human_view: Two orders in one sentence, and the second is the one that usually gets dropped. "Implement it" is the build; "use it" is the proof the build is real. A vault that is built and never operated is a museum — beautiful, empty, useless. The discipline in the middle is the sentence most teams skip: the design already exists, talked out and made beautiful, so the job is to find it in the record and implement THAT. Not a new invention, not a better idea found along the way — the design he already approved, built on the stack he named. And the honest limit is what keeps the order honest: the Supabase connector doc is a template with placeholders, not a working path. So the coordinator works out the real API path, verifies each step with a harmless read first, and whatever live key or deploy it cannot reach is his hand — not a workaround, not a quiet substitution. The key split has to live in the real system — RLS, Edge Functions, Cloudflare, the gate — because a split that lives only on paper is a promise, and promises are what the two keys were designed to replace.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you and a friend already drew the perfect plan for a treehouse — every board, every nail, all beautiful. Shawn says: don't draw a new plan. Build THAT plan, with the tools he named — and then actually play in the treehouse every day. Building it isn't enough; using it is the point.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn says the plan is already drawn and beautiful — so now build it, dear, with the tools he named, and then actually use it every day. A vault that's built but never used, dear, is just a pretty empty room. And one honest thing, dear: the instruction book for one of the tools is blank inside — so we work out the real way step by step, testing gently first, and whatever needs his hand, we bring to him.
intelligence.naya_view: IMPLEMENT IT AND USE IT. THE PRIOR DESIGN, BEAUTIFULLY TALKED OUT — NOT A NEW INVENTION. SUPABASE + CLOUDFLARE + GITHUB + NAYANET + THE BRIDGE.
